entries.name: AeroSandbox
entries.summary: Python aircraft design and optimization environment using automatic differentiation and composable engineering analyses. Useful for rapid aerodynamic design exploration and multidisciplinary studies before committing to higher-fidelity CFD evaluations.
entries.caveat: Many included methods are reduced-fidelity engineering models; do not equate all analyses with Navier–Stokes CFD.

metadata.description: Aircraft design optimization made fast through computational graph transformations (e.g., automatic differentiation). Composable analysis tools for aerodynamics, propulsion, structures, trajectory design, and much more.

entries.name: Chaospy
entries.summary: Numerical toolbox for polynomial chaos, sampling and quadrature. Useful for propagating uncertain flow parameters through CFD surrogates or moderately priced solvers and building nonintrusive uncertainty-expansion experiments.
entries.caveat: High-dimensional or discontinuous response surfaces may require alternatives to a simple polynomial expansion.

metadata.description: Chaospy - Toolbox for performing uncertainty quantification.

entries.name: Dakota
entries.summary: Design exploration framework combining optimization, parameter estimation, sensitivity analysis and uncertainty quantification. Useful for managing repeated CFD evaluations and propagating uncertain inputs through external engineering simulation models.
entries.caveat: Requires a working simulation interface and can demand many expensive flow evaluations.

metadata.description: The core Dakota project

entries.name: foamlib
entries.summary: Python interface for OpenFOAM files, cases and execution. Useful for reproducible parameter studies, programmatic field access and reducing repetitive case-management steps around an existing OpenFOAM installation.
entries.caveat: OpenFOAM must be installed separately; confirm support for the selected distribution and file types.

metadata.description: ✨ A modern Python package for interacting with OpenFOAM

entries.name: MPhys
entries.summary: Standardizes high-fidelity multiphysics problems within OpenMDAO using modular conventions and solver integrations. Useful for assembling CFD–structures or aerothermal studies while preserving coupling and derivative interfaces across disciplines.
entries.caveat: It is an integration layer; individual examples require compatible external solvers and their dependencies.

metadata.description: Multiphysics with OpenMDAO

entries.name: OpenMDAO
entries.summary: Python framework for tightly coupled systems analysis and multidisciplinary optimization. Useful for connecting CFD, structures and engineering models while managing derivatives, nonlinear coupling and parallel model execution.
entries.caveat: CFD analysis components and reliable derivatives must be supplied; it does not replace a flow solver.

metadata.description: OpenMDAO repository.

entries.name: OpenTURNS
entries.summary: C++ and Python library for probabilistic modelling and uncertainty treatment in industrial studies. Useful for wrapping CFD evaluations, defining uncertain inputs and constructing reliability, sensitivity or surrogate analyses.
entries.caveat: Physics and solver interfaces remain application-specific; verify sampling accuracy and assumptions about input distributions.

metadata.description: Probabilistic modelling and uncertainty quantification library

entries.name: pyOptSparse
entries.summary: Framework for defining and solving constrained nonlinear optimization problems with sparse derivatives. Useful as an optimization driver around aerodynamic CFD models and other expensive engineering analyses with many constraints.
entries.caveat: Some optimizer backends require separate proprietary licenses; check the chosen backend and installation.

metadata.description: pyOptSparse is an object-oriented framework for formulating and solving nonlinear constrained optimization problems in an efficient, reusable, and portable manner.

entries.name: RAVEN
entries.summary: Simulation workflow framework for uncertainty quantification, optimization, model reduction and probabilistic risk analysis. Useful for orchestrating external CFD studies, sampling parameter spaces and training surrogates around expensive evaluations.
entries.caveat: Requires model interfaces, configuration and domain-specific validation; probabilistic output is only as reliable as its assumptions.

metadata.description: RAVEN is a flexible and multi-purpose probabilistic risk analysis, validation and uncertainty quantification, parameter optimization, model reduction and data knowledge-discovering framework.

entries.name: SALib
entries.summary: Python implementations of global sensitivity-analysis methods such as Sobol and Morris. Useful for ranking uncertain CFD inputs after sampling and evaluating a separate solver or surrogate model.
entries.caveat: Generates designs and analyzes outputs; the user supplies solver runs and checks estimator convergence.

metadata.description: Sensitivity Analysis Library in Python. Contains Sobol, Morris, FAST, and other methods.

entries.name: UQpy
entries.summary: General Python toolbox for modelling uncertainty in physical and mathematical systems. Useful for uncertainty propagation and surrogate-based analyses around CFD models when sampling and probabilistic workflows need programmable control.
entries.caveat: A general UQ library rather than a CFD package; connect and validate the simulation model separately.

metadata.description: UQpy (Uncertainty Quantification with python) is a general purpose Python toolbox for modeling uncertainty in physical and mathematical systems.

entries.name: DAFoam
entries.summary: Adds discrete-adjoint capabilities to OpenFOAM-based multiphysics analysis with a Python interface for optimization. Supports aerodynamic, thermal and coupled design studies with many design variables.
entries.caveat: Requires compatible OpenFOAM and optimization dependencies; convergence of the primal and adjoint problems matters for usable design gradients. Use the documented solver and dependency versions; verify adjoint gradients for the chosen objective and case.

metadata.description: DAFoam: Discrete Adjoint with OpenFOAM for High-fidelity Multidisciplinary Design Optimization

entries.name: DuMux
entries.summary: Models porous-medium flow, transport and deformation with finite-volume and control-volume finite-element methods. Includes coupled multidomain formulations for applications that cross free-flow and porous regions.
entries.caveat: The GitHub repository is an official mirror; primary development and issue tracking are hosted by the Stuttgart GitLab project.

metadata.description: DuMux: an open-source simulator for flow and transport processes in porous media (repository mirrored from https://git.iws.uni-stuttgart.de/dumux-repositories/dumux.git)

entries.name: IBAMR
entries.summary: Combines immersed-boundary methods with Cartesian adaptive mesh refinement and distributed-memory parallelism. Useful for deformable structures interacting with fluids while retaining separate Eulerian and Lagrangian descriptions.
entries.caveat: Requires a substantial numerical-library stack; discretization and coupling choices must match the stiffness, resolution and boundary conditions of the problem.

metadata.description: An adaptive and distributed-memory parallel implementation of the immersed boundary (IB) method

entries.name: MRST
entries.summary: Provides a MATLAB toolbox for flow, transport and mechanics in porous media. Includes modular reservoir and carbon-storage workflows that support numerical experimentation and model development.
entries.caveat: Upstream recommends packaged releases for most users; compatibility with GNU Octave varies by module and should not be assumed.

metadata.description: Official GitHub repository for MRST - the MATLAB Reservoir Simulation Toolbox

entries.name: oomph-lib
entries.summary: Offers an object-oriented finite-element library with extensive multiphysics demonstration problems. Useful for building fluid-mechanics and fluid-structure models when researchers need control of the governing formulation.
entries.caveat: A programmable numerical library rather than a turnkey engineering interface; model formulation and solver choices remain the user's responsibility.

metadata.description: An object-oriented, open-source finite-element library for the simulation of multi-physics problems

entries.name: OpenPNM
entries.summary: Represents porous materials as pore networks and solves transport across them. Useful when investigating effective flow and transport properties without directly resolving every pore-scale fluid volume.
entries.caveat: Network representations simplify pore geometry and physics; they are not interchangeable with fully resolved pore-scale Navier-Stokes simulations.

metadata.description: A Python package for performing pore network modeling of porous media

entries.name: OPM Flow
entries.summary: Implements reservoir flow simulation with automatic differentiation and established reservoir input formats. Useful for multiphase subsurface studies that need well models and reservoir-scale fluid transport.
entries.caveat: Reservoir models operate under subsurface-flow assumptions and should not be substituted directly for free-fluid CFD.

metadata.description: OPM Flow and experimental simulators, including components such as well models etc.

entries.name: preCICE
entries.summary: Connects existing simulation programs through partitioned coupling, interface data exchange and mapping. Provides a common route to fluid-structure interaction, conjugate heat transfer and other coupled workflows.
entries.caveat: A coupling library, not a CFD solver. Stable coupling still depends on compatible adapters, interface conditions and convergence settings.

metadata.description: A coupling library and ecosystem for partitioned multi-physics and multi-scale simulations, including surface and volume coupling.

entries.name: solids4foam
entries.summary: Extends the OpenFOAM ecosystem with solid-mechanics and fluid-solid interaction models. Provides tutorials for comparing partitioned coupling approaches and examining deformation-driven changes to a flow domain.
entries.caveat: Compatibility is OpenFOAM-version dependent; verify the supported fork and version rather than mixing tutorial generations.

metadata.description: The official repository for solids4foam

entries.name: svMultiPhysics
entries.summary: Provides coupled finite-element models for fluids, solids, diffusion and electrophysiology in cardiovascular research. Supports investigations where blood flow and deforming biological tissue must be modeled together.
entries.caveat: Formerly svFSIplus; research software does not itself establish clinical suitability. Patient-specific predictions require separate validation and appropriate expertise.

metadata.description: svMultiPhysics is an open-source, parallel, finite element multi-physics solver.

entries.name: ADCIRC
entries.summary: Models time-dependent free-surface circulation and transport on unstructured finite-element grids. Common application areas include storm surge, tides, wind-driven circulation and coastal flooding studies.
entries.caveat: Requires suitable meshes, forcing and calibration for the site; official documentation is being consolidated across several maintained sources.

metadata.description: ADCIRC Model Repository

entries.name: ANUGA
entries.summary: Solves shallow-water equations for floods, tsunamis and storm surges using finite-volume methods. Provides Python workflows and examples for combining terrain, boundary conditions and inundation studies.
entries.caveat: Depth-averaged shallow-water assumptions do not resolve detailed vertical flow structure; terrain and boundary-data quality strongly affect inundation results.

metadata.description: ANUGA: open-source hydrodynamic modelling of floods, tsunamis and storm surges (shallow water equations, finite volumes). GPU/multicore solver developed with C-DAC (India) and NCI (Australia).

entries.name: CM1
entries.summary: Supports idealized atmospheric experiments with a nonhydrostatic numerical model. Useful for studying convection, clouds and organized storms while controlling the background state and experimental forcing.
entries.caveat: Primarily an idealized research model; configuring a real-time operational forecast is a different task from running its standard experiments.

metadata.description: Cloud Model 1 (CM1), a numerical model for idealized studies of the atmosphere written by George Bryan

entries.name: Delft3D
entries.summary: Collects Delft3D structured and flexible-mesh simulation engines for hydrodynamics, waves, morphology and water quality. Useful for integrated coastal, estuarine, river and urban water studies.
entries.caveat: The source engines and packaged graphical interfaces have different delivery arrangements; component licensing and build requirements should be checked individually.

metadata.description: Repository for Delft3D FM and Delft3D 4 kernels

entries.name: ERF
entries.summary: Builds atmospheric-flow modeling on AMReX with adaptive meshes and a documented theory and examples. Relevant to energy-related atmospheric research and simulations requiring local resolution refinement.
entries.caveat: Check the supported atmospheric models and boundary treatments for the intended application; the solver remains an evolving research code.

metadata.description: Energy Research and Forecasting Model

entries.name: FUNWAVE-TVD
entries.summary: Models dispersive nearshore waves with a Boussinesq-type formulation and shock-capturing treatment. Useful for wave transformation, coastal wave generation and studying processes beyond nondispersive shallow-water models.
entries.caveat: Upstream labels the default branch beta and directs users to released versions. Confirm licensing and the release appropriate to your study.

entries.name: GeoClaw
entries.summary: Extends Clawpack for geophysical waves and flows, including tsunami propagation and inundation. Uses adaptive refinement to concentrate resolution where evolving waves and coastal interactions require it.
entries.caveat: Depth-averaged flow assumptions and topographic resolution constrain the phenomena represented; assess the model for the intended hazard application.

metadata.description: Version of Clawpack for geophysical waves and flows

entries.name: Kynema-SGF (formerly AMR-Wind)
entries.summary: Uses an adaptive structured-grid incompressible formulation for atmospheric boundary layers and wind-farm wakes. Can serve as the background flow solver in coupled blade-resolved wind-energy simulations.
entries.best_for: Wind-farm wakes and atmospheric boundary layers
entries.caveat: Renamed from AMR-Wind in 2026; actuator models and blade-resolved overset configurations represent different levels of physical detail.

metadata.description: AMReX-based structured grid fluid solver

entries.name: Kynema-UGF (formerly Nalu-Wind)
entries.summary: Provides an unstructured incompressible flow solver used in the Kynema wind-energy ecosystem. Useful for geometry-resolved turbine and energy-system flow calculations alongside structured background simulations.
entries.caveat: Renamed from Nalu-Wind in 2026; coupled overset studies require additional ecosystem components and matching configuration.

metadata.description: Unstructured grid fluid solver for the Kynema project

entries.name: MITgcm
entries.summary: Models ocean and atmospheric circulation with a configurable numerical core and extensive verification examples. Useful across geophysical scales, including nonhydrostatic ocean processes and large-scale circulation.
entries.best_for: Ocean circulation and geophysical fluid dynamics
entries.caveat: Configuration, forcing and parameterizations determine the applicable scale; reproducing an experiment requires more than selecting a solver executable.

metadata.description: M.I.T General Circulation Model master code and documentation repository

entries.name: MOM6
entries.summary: Solves ocean primitive equations with flexible vertical coordinates and options for coupled Earth-system configurations. Useful for ocean circulation studies and research into ocean-model numerics and parameterizations.
entries.caveat: Designed for ocean primitive-equation modeling rather than general free-surface engineering CFD; regional setups need appropriate forcing and boundary data.

metadata.description: Modular Ocean Model

entries.name: MPAS-Model
entries.summary: Provides a shared unstructured-mesh framework with atmosphere, ocean and other geophysical model cores. Useful for multiscale circulation studies where mesh design and regional refinement matter.
entries.caveat: Individual cores have separate build instructions, capabilities and data requirements; the shared repository is not a single universal model.

metadata.description: Repository for MPAS models and shared framework releases.

entries.name: Proteus
entries.summary: Separates continuum physical models from numerical methods in a Python-led toolkit. Includes multiphase Navier-Stokes, shallow-water and porous-flow formulations relevant to hydraulic and coastal research.
entries.caveat: Broad method availability does not make every formulation suitable for every problem; external compiled dependencies are part of the installation.

metadata.description: A computational methods and simulation toolkit

entries.name: SCHISM
entries.summary: Uses unstructured grids for three-dimensional baroclinic circulation across connected river, estuary, shelf and ocean scales. Useful when one study spans several interacting hydrodynamic environments.
entries.caveat: Choose supported modules and document forcing and vertical-grid assumptions; development-branch flags can change between model versions.

metadata.description: Semi-implicit Cross-scale Hydroscience Integrated System Model (SCHISM)

entries.name: Thetis
entries.summary: Builds coastal and estuarine flow models on Firedrake finite elements. Includes shallow-water, tracer, wetting-and-drying and adjoint capabilities for studying circulation and inverse problems.
entries.caveat: Development versions may require matching Firedrake development branches; shallow-water assumptions must fit the intended physical scales.

metadata.description: Finite element flow solver for simulating coastal and estuarine flows.

entries.name: WRF
entries.summary: Provides the Weather Research and Forecasting modeling system for atmospheric research and numerical weather prediction. Useful when CFD studies need meteorological context or mesoscale flow conditions.
entries.caveat: Meteorological predictions depend on initialization, forcing and physical parameterizations; WRF is not a replacement for geometry-resolved local engineering CFD.

metadata.description: The official repository for the Weather Research and Forecasting (WRF) model

entries.name: ADflow
entries.summary: Compressible Euler, laminar Navier-Stokes and RANS solver on structured multiblock and overset meshes, with a discrete adjoint and derivative-verification facilities for aerodynamic design optimization.
entries.caveat: Targets structured and overset design workflows; a mesh generator and the surrounding MDO dependencies may be required for complete optimization studies.

metadata.description: ADflow is a finite volume RANS solver tailored for gradient-based aerodynamic design optimization.

entries.name: code_saturne
entries.summary: EDF's general-purpose CFD system for industrial flow and transport studies, providing finite-volume numerics, turbulence and heat-transfer models, parallel execution, and associated case setup tooling.
entries.caveat: The project describes this GitHub repository as its public mirror; follow official release and contribution instructions rather than treating every branch as a release.

metadata.description: code_saturne public mirror

entries.name: COOLFluiD
entries.summary: Object-oriented high-performance platform for computational fluid dynamics, plasma and multiphysics simulations, exposing a modular research environment for developing and combining numerical methods and physical models.
entries.caveat: Check the relevant plugin documentation and licensing details; this is a developer-oriented platform with a substantial build configuration.

metadata.description: The object-oriented HPC platform for CFD, plasma and multi-physics simulations whose development started in 2002 at the Von Karman Institute for Fluid Dynamics is finally open!

entries.name: Elmer FEM
entries.summary: Multiphysics finite-element package combining fluid mechanics, heat transfer and other field solvers, with mesh and graphical tools plus parallel infrastructure for coupled scientific simulations.
entries.caveat: Select the solver module, discretization and coupling strategy explicitly; breadth of available physics does not imply every coupling is turnkey.

metadata.description: Official git repository of Elmer FEM software

entries.name: FiPy
entries.summary: Python finite-volume PDE framework from NIST for assembling coupled convection, diffusion, transient and source terms, particularly useful for transport, phase-field and materials-model prototyping and research.
entries.caveat: A PDE-building framework rather than a complete industrial Navier-Stokes workflow; users must formulate and verify their coupled equations.

metadata.description: FiPy is a Finite Volume PDE solver written in Python

entries.name: Fluidity
entries.summary: Unstructured finite-element and control-volume CFD code with anisotropic mesh adaptivity, parallel execution and Python interfaces, used for multiphase, geophysical and general fluid-dynamics simulations.
entries.caveat: The dependency and platform setup is substantial; use installation instructions matching the chosen branch and environment.

metadata.description: Fluidity

entries.name: Kratos Multiphysics
entries.summary: Modular C++ multiphysics framework with Python interfaces and dedicated fluid-dynamics, fluid-structure interaction and particle applications, supporting coupled engineering workflows and parallel simulation development.
entries.caveat: Capabilities belong to specific applications; the core framework alone is not a configured CFD solver.

metadata.description: Kratos Multiphysics (A.K.A Kratos) is a framework for building parallel multi-disciplinary simulation software. Modularity, extensibility and HPC are the main objectives. Kratos has BSD license and is written in C++ with extensive Python interface.

entries.name: Lethe
entries.summary: Finite-element CFD and discrete-element project using deal.II, with high-order continuous Galerkin formulations, adaptive meshes and coupled fluid-particle solvers for single-phase and multiphase engineering research.
entries.caveat: Requires a compatible deal.II dependency stack; choose the relevant solver and reproduce its documented benchmark before extending a model.

metadata.description: Repository for the open-source lethe CFD/DEM/CFD-DEM project

entries.name: MOOSE Navier-Stokes
entries.summary: Navier-Stokes module within the MOOSE multiphysics framework, offering finite-element and finite-volume formulations for pressure-based, compressible and porous-flow applications with shared nonlinear-solver infrastructure and coupling mechanisms.
entries.caveat: Read the module's solver-capability matrix: turbulence, two-phase and compressibility support varies between formulations and is actively evolving.

metadata.description: Multiphysics Object Oriented Simulation Environment: A robust, modern, extendable, finite element/finite volume framework that excels at creating complex multiphysics simulations.

entries.name: OpenFOAM Foundation
entries.summary: Finite-volume CFD platform with an extensive solver, physical-model and meshing ecosystem, covering incompressible and compressible flows, turbulence, heat transfer, reacting systems and multiphase problems.
entries.caveat: Foundation development branch; use a release for a fixed baseline. OpenCFD's separately maintained OpenFOAM distribution has a different upstream and release scheme.

metadata.description: OpenFOAM Foundation development repository

entries.name: SU2
entries.summary: Multiphysics analysis and design suite centered on CFD and aerodynamic optimization, combining flow solvers, adjoint methods and Python-driven workflows for PDE-constrained engineering design studies.
entries.caveat: Check the configuration and physical-model support for the specific SU2 release; example coverage does not establish accuracy for a new design.

metadata.description: SU2: An Open-Source Suite for Multiphysics Simulation and Design

entries.name: CadQuery
entries.summary: Python-based parametric CAD scripting built on Open CASCADE. Parameterized channels, nozzles and mechanical components can be generated consistently for geometry sweeps, automated studies and downstream mesh preparation.
entries.caveat: Provides geometry construction rather than a CFD mesher or solver.

metadata.description: A python parametric CAD scripting framework based on OCCT

entries.name: CGAL
entries.summary: Computational geometry algorithms for triangulation, surface processing and mesh generation. Supplies robust geometric building blocks for custom CFD preprocessing tools rather than a single ready-made flow-analysis workflow.
entries.caveat: License terms differ by CGAL package; check the specific component before integration.

metadata.description: The public CGAL repository, see the README below

entries.name: FreeCAD
entries.summary: Parametric solid modelling for engineering geometry, with editable design history and interoperable CAD workflows. Useful for preparing and revising fluid-domain boundaries before meshing rather than solving flow.
entries.caveat: A CAD model is not automatically a watertight or appropriately resolved CFD domain.

metadata.description: Official source code of FreeCAD, a free and opensource multiplatform 3D parametric modeler.

entries.name: IDWarp
entries.summary: Deforms volume mesh nodes in response to surface perturbations using an inverse-distance approach. Useful for reusing a baseline CFD mesh during aerodynamic shape optimization and sensitivity calculations.
entries.caveat: Large surface changes can still produce poor-quality or invalid cells; monitor mesh quality.

metadata.description: IDWarp is a mesh warping package for the MACH framework.

entries.name: meshio
entries.summary: Reads and writes many mesh formats through Python and a command-line interface. Helps move geometry, cells and associated fields between meshing tools, numerical solvers and visualization software.
entries.caveat: Not every format preserves every field, boundary convention or high-order element representation.

metadata.description: :spider_web: input/output for many mesh formats

entries.name: Netgen
entries.summary: Automatic tetrahedral mesh generation from constructive geometry, STL surfaces and CAD geometry. Python scripting, refinement and optimization make it useful for reproducible finite-element flow preprocessing.
entries.caveat: Mesh topology, boundary tagging and wall-resolution requirements still need solver-specific checking.

entries.name: pygalmesh
entries.summary: Python interface to CGAL's mesh-generation capabilities, including primitive and implicit domains. Useful for constructing tetrahedral meshes from mathematical geometries and exporting them for numerical PDE experiments.
entries.caveat: Sharp intersections and detailed meshing controls need care; this is not a CAD repair application.

metadata.description: :spider_web: A Python interface to CGAL's meshing tools

entries.name: pyGeo
entries.summary: Geometry parameterization and geometric constraints for multidisciplinary optimization. Free-form deformation, CAD interfaces and design-variable handling connect aerodynamic shape changes to repeatable CFD and coupled engineering studies.
entries.caveat: Individual CAD interfaces introduce their own installation and licensing requirements.

metadata.description: pyGeo provides geometric design variables and constraints suitable for gradient-based optimization.

entries.name: pygmsh
entries.summary: Python geometry helpers around Gmsh reduce repetitive low-level entity bookkeeping. Useful for creating parameterized two- and three-dimensional domains and exporting meshes into automated numerical experiments.
entries.caveat: Requires Gmsh; native Gmsh features and version compatibility should be checked for advanced workflows.

metadata.description: :spider_web: Gmsh for Python

entries.name: pyHyp
entries.summary: Extrudes structured surface meshes into volume meshes using hyperbolic marching. Designed for the preprocessing stage of aerodynamic optimization workflows where body-fitted structured grids and controlled extrusion are useful.
entries.caveat: Needs a suitable structured surface mesh; it is not an arbitrary-geometry unstructured mesher.

metadata.description: pyHyp generates volume meshes from surface meshes using hyperbolic marching.

entries.name: SALOME SMESH
entries.summary: SALOME's mesh module creates, edits, imports and exports computational meshes, with grouping, quality controls and geometry integration. Supports preprocessing pipelines needing interactive inspection alongside structured automation.
entries.best_for: Interactive mesh preparation and quality checks
entries.caveat: Building the module requires additional SALOME components; the repository is not a standalone application installer.

metadata.description: Salome MESH (SMESH) module to create and edit mesh in SALOME platform

entries.name: trimesh
entries.summary: Python tools for loading, inspecting and manipulating triangular surfaces. Helpful for checking imported STL geometry, connectivity and surface properties before committing to expensive volume meshing or flow calculations.
entries.caveat: Surface processing does not establish CAD fidelity or the adequacy of a CFD boundary-layer mesh.

metadata.description: Python library for loading and using triangular meshes.

entries.name: ExaDG
entries.summary: Matrix-free high-order discontinuous Galerkin project whose core incompressible Navier-Stokes solver targets LES and DNS, with additional flow-transport, moving-mesh, fluid-structure and compressible-flow capabilities for research applications.
entries.caveat: Best aligned with quadrilateral/hexahedral high-order discretizations; installation requires a compatible finite-element and linear-algebra dependency stack.

metadata.description: ExaDG - High-Order Discontinuous Galerkin for the Exa-Scale

entries.name: FLEXI
entries.summary: Discontinuous Galerkin spectral-element framework for hyperbolic-parabolic conservation laws, emphasizing compressible CFD on unstructured hexahedral meshes with parallel execution and a supporting preprocessing and postprocessing suite.
entries.caveat: Uses a specific high-order mesh and preprocessing workflow; check the required HOPR and HDF5 versions for the chosen release.

metadata.description: FLEXI: A high order discontinuous Galerkin framework for hyperbolic–parabolic conservation laws

entries.name: HORSES3D
entries.summary: Fortran DG spectral-element multiphysics solver for compressible and incompressible flows, with polynomial adaptivity, turbulence closures and diffuse-interface multiphase formulations on curvilinear hexahedral meshes using hybrid CPU parallelism.
entries.caveat: The CPU repository and separate GPU project have different supported paths; verify that a desired feature is available in the selected implementation.

metadata.description: HORSES3D: A high-order discontinuous Galerkin solver for flow simulations and multi-physics applications

entries.name: MIRGE-Com
entries.summary: Python-driven discontinuous Galerkin simulation application for compressible viscous and inviscid reactive mixtures, using unstructured meshes and accelerator-oriented infrastructure for exascale-enabled scramjet and fluid-flow research.
entries.best_for: Research on reacting compressible DG solvers
entries.caveat: Research application with a specialized array, mesh and code-generation stack; inspect supported chemistry and transport assumptions before selecting it for a study.

metadata.description: MIRGE-Com is the workhorse simulation application for the Center for Exascale-Enabled Scramjet Design at the University of Illinois.

entries.name: Nek5000
entries.summary: Spectral-element solver for incompressible and low-Mach flows, scalar transport and conjugate heat transfer, using high-order tensor-product elements and parallel algorithms suited to turbulence research.
entries.best_for: High-order incompressible DNS and heat transfer
entries.caveat: Classic CPU-oriented Nek implementation; mesh and polynomial resolution must be selected for the intended flow and turbulence regime.

metadata.description: our classic

entries.name: nekRS
entries.summary: High-order spectral-element CFD solver for incompressible and low-Mach flow, with OCCA-based CPU and GPU backends, scalar transport, turbulence models and conjugate heat-transfer capabilities on HPC systems.
entries.caveat: Follow the release notes and backend requirements; the project distinguishes stable master from preview development and does not support every desktop platform.

metadata.description: next generation fast and scalable CFD code

entries.name: PyFR
entries.summary: Flux-reconstruction CFD platform for high-order scale-resolving flow simulations on unstructured mixed-element meshes, with code-generated computational kernels and multiple CPU and GPU execution backends for heterogeneous systems.
entries.caveat: Backend, mesh-element and equation-system support depend on the selected release; compare cost at equivalent accuracy rather than polynomial order alone.

metadata.description: PyFR

entries.name: Trixi.jl
entries.summary: Julia framework for high-order conservation-law simulations, combining discontinuous Galerkin and related methods, adaptive tree-based meshes and an extensible equation interface for compressible-flow and numerical-method research.
entries.caveat: Check equation, mesh and backend compatibility in the documentation; Julia's first-run compilation cost should be separated from steady-state timings.

metadata.description: Trixi.jl: Adaptive high-order numerical simulations of conservation laws in Julia

entries.name: UCNS3D
entries.summary: Unstructured compressible-flow solver offering high-order finite-volume reconstruction and discontinuous Galerkin methods, mixed-element meshes, turbulence models and MPI/OpenMP execution for aerodynamic and multicomponent-flow research in two or three dimensions.
entries.best_for: High-order compressible CFD on mixed meshes
entries.caveat: Build bounds can be case-specific, and accelerator offload covers selected paths rather than every solver mode; follow the current build instructions.

metadata.description: Unstructured Compressible Navier Stokes 3D code (UCNS3D)

entries.name: DualSPHysics
entries.summary: Smoothed-particle hydrodynamics solver using C++, CUDA and OpenMP, with engineering workflows focused on free surfaces, wave interactions and large-deformation fluid motion around moving bodies and structures.
entries.caveat: The complete user distribution includes associated tools beyond the source repository; particle resolution, artificial compressibility and boundary treatment require case-specific assessment. Particle resolution, boundary treatment and weak-compressibility settings influence results; GPU builds require a supported CUDA toolchain.

metadata.description: C++/CUDA/OpenMP based Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics (SPH) Solver

entries.name: FluidX3D
entries.summary: OpenCL lattice-Boltzmann flow simulator with CPU and GPU execution, integrated visualization, free-surface and thermal extensions, and tools for importing triangulated geometry into a Cartesian lattice for interactive studies.
entries.caveat: Source-available with a non-commercial restriction, explicitly not OSI open source. Check its current license before use; the documented solver has no checkpoint/restart support.

metadata.description: The fastest and most memory efficient lattice Boltzmann CFD software, running on all GPUs and CPUs via OpenCL. Free for non-commercial use.

entries.name: GPUSPH
entries.summary: CUDA implementation of weakly compressible smoothed-particle hydrodynamics, providing GPU-oriented infrastructure for free-surface flow simulations and research involving moving boundaries and fluid interactions with engineering geometries.
entries.caveat: CUDA hardware and a compatible compiler stack are required; establish the chosen formulation's resolution and compressibility error for the case.

metadata.description: The world's first CUDA implementation of Weakly-Compressible Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics

entries.name: HemoCell
entries.summary: Cell-resolved suspension framework coupling Palabos lattice-Boltzmann fluid dynamics to deformable Lagrangian cell membranes through immersed boundaries, with dedicated models and parallel data management for blood-flow research.
entries.caveat: A specialized cellular-flow model, not a clinical prediction tool; inspect cell mechanics, material parameters and case-specific validation requirements.

metadata.description: HemoCell is a high-performance suspension code for simulating blood flows developed by the Computational Science Lab at the University of Amsterdam.

entries.name: Lettuce
entries.summary: PyTorch-based lattice-Boltzmann framework for two- and three-dimensional fluid simulations, enabling Python prototyping, GPU execution and experiments connecting kinetic flow solvers with neural networks and automatic differentiation.
entries.caveat: Check current PyTorch/CUDA compatibility and whether custom kernels support the intended differentiable workflow; default installation targets specific CUDA versions.

metadata.description: Computational Fluid Dynamics based on PyTorch and the Lattice Boltzmann Method

entries.name: NATriuM
entries.summary: High-order off-lattice Boltzmann research solver based on deal.II, supporting unstructured two- and three-dimensional grids through discontinuous-Galerkin or semi-Lagrangian streaming for weakly and fully compressible viscous flows.
entries.caveat: Authors explicitly warn that the code is early-stage and they are unlikely to answer questions; treat it as a research reference with limited support.

metadata.description: High-order semi-Lagrangian/finite element lattice Boltzmann solver based on deal.ii

entries.name: PySPH
entries.summary: Python framework for defining particle equations and integrators, generating compiled Cython or OpenCL kernels, and running several SPH formulations with optional shared-memory and distributed parallelism for research simulations.
entries.caveat: Different bundled SPH formulations make different assumptions; compare conservation, convergence and boundary behavior for the scheme actually used. A method-development framework: selecting an available formulation does not establish suitability for a particular engineering problem.

metadata.description: A framework for Smoothed Particle Hydrodynamics in Python

entries.name: Sailfish
entries.summary: GPU lattice-Boltzmann simulation package with a Python-driven setup and CUDA or OpenCL execution, providing examples for exploring kinetic flow models and generated computational kernels on supported accelerators.
entries.caveat: Legacy dependency and GPU-toolchain assumptions need checking before adoption; its historical examples should not be assumed compatible with a current Python environment.

metadata.description: Lattice Boltzmann (LBM) simulation package for GPUs (CUDA, OpenCL)

entries.name: SPHinXsys
entries.summary: C++ multiphysics library built around smoothed-particle hydrodynamics, providing unified discretizations and strongly coupled fluid, solid and multibody models together with examples and a Python interface for engineering studies.
entries.caveat: Select the specific formulation and tested example family; a common particle framework does not eliminate resolution or coupling-error studies. Research and engineering library with model-specific assumptions; choose examples matching the intended constitutive laws and flow regime.

metadata.description: SPHinXsys provides C++ APIs for engineering simulation and optimization. It aims at complex systems driven by fluid, structure, multi-body dynamics and beyond. The multi-physics library is based on a unique and unified computational framework by which strong coupling has been achieved for all involved physics.

entries.name: DAPPER
entries.summary: Experimental data-assimilation framework with ensemble and variational methods, diagnostics and model examples. Useful for learning state estimation and testing assimilation ideas on geophysical-fluid prototypes before solver-specific integration.
entries.caveat: Designed for teaching and fundamental experiments; coupling production CFD requires additional implementation.

metadata.description: Data Assimilation with Python: a Package for Experimental Research

entries.name: DeepXDE
entries.summary: Scientific machine-learning library supporting physics-informed networks and neural operators. Includes differential-equation workflows useful for fluid inverse problems, parameter estimation and exploratory surrogate studies with explicit boundary and initial conditions.
entries.caveat: PINN training convergence is problem dependent; verify predictions against trusted numerical or experimental references.

metadata.description: A library for scientific machine learning and physics-informed learning

entries.name: EZyRB
entries.summary: Data-driven reduced-basis modelling from parameterized numerical snapshots. Useful for constructing nonintrusive CFD surrogates when full-order results are available but modifying the original governing-equation implementation is impractical.
entries.caveat: Prediction quality depends on snapshot coverage; extrapolation beyond the training parameter range needs testing.

metadata.description: Easy Reduced Basis method

entries.name: ITHACA-FV
entries.summary: OpenFOAM-based reduced-order-modelling framework with methods for developing compact finite-volume models. Useful for experimenting with projection, parameterized flow snapshots and reduced solvers close to existing OpenFOAM workflows.
entries.caveat: Check the supported OpenFOAM release and rebuild dependencies for the selected branch.

metadata.description: Reduced order modelling techniques for OpenFOAM

entries.name: NeuralOperator
entries.summary: Official neural-operator library containing Fourier Neural Operators and related architectures. Useful for learning mappings between PDE inputs and solution fields, including fluid and transport surrogate research.
entries.caveat: Resolution transfer does not guarantee accuracy under new geometries, regimes or boundary conditions.

metadata.description: Learning in infinite dimension with neural operators.

entries.name: NVIDIA PhysicsNeMo
entries.summary: PyTorch-based physics machine-learning framework with reusable models and training recipes. Aerodynamics examples make it relevant to surface and volume surrogates, scalable training and engineering field prediction.
entries.caveat: GPU requirements, model prerequisites and separate dataset terms vary across examples.

metadata.description: Open-source deep-learning framework for building, training, and fine-tuning deep learning models using state-of-the-art Physics-ML methods

entries.name: PDEArena
entries.summary: Training and evaluation framework for neural PDE modelling, with architecture collections and fluid datasets. Useful for controlled comparisons of learned Navier–Stokes and shallow-water evolution models across spatial and temporal scales.
entries.caveat: Research benchmarks and trained models do not establish performance on industrial geometries or operating regimes.

entries.name: PhiFlow
entries.summary: Differentiable simulation toolkit integrated with NumPy and machine-learning frameworks. Provides fluid examples and automatic differentiation pathways useful for inverse problems, learned corrections and optimization through simulations.
entries.caveat: Choose the numerical model and discretization for the intended physics; differentiability alone does not establish fidelity.

metadata.description: A differentiable PDE solving framework for machine learning

entries.name: PyDMD
entries.summary: Dynamic mode decomposition tools for extracting coherent spatial and temporal structures from snapshot data. Useful for analyzing CFD transients, building data-driven reduced models and comparing modal representations.
entries.caveat: Mode estimates depend on sampling, noise and preprocessing; the fitted dynamics need independent validation.

metadata.description: Python Dynamic Mode Decomposition

entries.name: pyMOR
entries.summary: Model-order-reduction library using abstract interfaces to connect numerical algorithms and PDE backends. Supports reduced bases, POD and system-theoretic approaches for constructing compact parameterized flow or transport models.
entries.caveat: Connecting a new CFD solver requires compatible operators, data access and suitable reduction assumptions.

metadata.description: pyMOR - Model Order Reduction with Python

entries.name: PySINDy
entries.summary: Sparse system-identification tools for discovering compact dynamical models from data. Useful for fluid reduced coordinates and PDE-discovery experiments where interpretable model structure is preferable to a black-box surrogate.
entries.caveat: Derivative estimation, noise and candidate-library choices strongly affect discovered equations.

metadata.description: A package for the sparse identification of nonlinear dynamical systems from data

entries.name: Transolver
entries.summary: Research implementation of transformer-based PDE modelling on general geometries. Includes airfoil and car-flow design experiments, making it useful for studying geometry-aware surrogates alongside established neural-operator baselines.
entries.caveat: Published benchmark claims belong to the original study; reproduce the selected task before relying on generalization.

metadata.description: About code release of "Transolver: A Fast Transformer Solver for PDEs on General Geometries", ICML 2024 Spotlight. https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.02366

entries.name: CFDEM coupling PUBLIC
entries.summary: Couples OpenFOAM flow calculations with discrete particle dynamics through selectable force and data-exchange models. Useful for studying fluidized beds, particulate transport and fluid-particle interaction workflows.
entries.caveat: Public and commercial product capabilities differ. Verify the documented OpenFOAM and particle-solver versions before installation.

metadata.description: latest version of CFDEM®coupling toolbox, released by DCS Computing GmbH

entries.name: JAX-Fluids
entries.summary: Implements differentiable compressible flow simulation with high-order reconstruction, level-set and diffuse-interface two-phase methods. Enables research connecting numerical fluid dynamics, automatic differentiation and accelerator-based computation.
entries.caveat: Differentiating a discrete solver does not automatically yield reliable gradients through shocks or interface events; examine discretization and sensitivity assumptions.

metadata.description: Differentiable Fluid Dynamics Package

entries.name: Mantaflow
entries.summary: Combines a fluid-simulation core with Python scene definitions and an extensible plugin system. Supports liquid, smoke and learning experiments aimed at graphics-oriented fluid algorithm research.
entries.caveat: Designed primarily for computer-graphics research; attractive visual output alone does not establish engineering accuracy.

metadata.description: mantaflow is an open-source framework targeted at fluid simulation research in Computer Graphics and Machine Learning.

entries.name: MFC
entries.summary: Solves compressible multiphase flows with interface models, bubble dynamics, phase-change options and particle tracking. Useful for investigating shock-interface interaction and other strongly compressible multiphase phenomena.
entries.caveat: Different mixture, interface and bubble models make different assumptions; select the model appropriate to the physical scale and regime.

metadata.description: Exascale multiphase flow solver — 2025 Gordon Bell Prize Finalist | 200T grid points on 43K+ GPUs

entries.name: SPlisHSPlasH
entries.summary: Implements several incompressible SPH pressure solvers alongside viscosity, surface tension and rigid or deformable body coupling. Particularly useful for comparing particle-fluid simulation methods and visual experiments.
entries.best_for: SPH incompressibility and coupled particle scenes
entries.caveat: Originates in physically based graphics research; engineering use needs independent dimensional, resolution and validation checks.

metadata.description: SPlisHSPlasH is an open-source library for the physically-based simulation of fluids.

entries.name: ABLATE
entries.summary: Develops reacting-flow capabilities around turbulent mixing, fuel entrainment and ablative boundary layers. Offers a research entry point for studying combustion environments associated with hybrid rocket motors.
entries.caveat: Research-oriented software; use documented examples and confirm the available physical models before planning a new application.

metadata.description: ABLATE is a UB CHREST project focused on leveraging advances in both exascale computing and machine learning to better understand the turbulent mixing and fuel entrainment in the combustion environment that is critical to the operation of hybrid rocket motors.

entries.name: Cantera
entries.summary: Provides thermochemistry, transport properties, reaction mechanisms, reactor networks and one-dimensional flames. A practical foundation for checking chemistry assumptions before embedding them in a reacting-flow solver.
entries.caveat: Not a general three-dimensional CFD solver; mechanism suitability must be assessed for the intended conditions.

metadata.description: Chemical kinetics, thermodynamics, and transport tool suite

entries.name: Fire Dynamics Simulator
entries.summary: Models low-speed fire-driven flows with large-eddy simulation, emphasizing smoke and heat transport. Its documentation includes separate verification and validation material for assessing intended fire-engineering applications.
entries.caveat: A low-speed fire model rather than a general shock or detonation solver. Safety-critical conclusions require qualified interpretation and appropriate validation.

metadata.description: Fire Dynamics Simulator

entries.name: PeleC
entries.summary: Solves compressible reacting flows using block-structured adaptive meshes and embedded boundaries. Connects detailed chemistry to flow calculations where acoustic waves and compressibility are physically important.
entries.caveat: Requires the AMReX, PelePhysics and SUNDIALS stack; mesh, chemistry and temporal resolution need problem-specific assessment.

metadata.description: An AMR code for compressible reacting flow simulations

entries.name: PeleLMeX
entries.summary: Combines a low-Mach reacting-flow formulation with adaptive refinement and embedded boundaries. Targets flame-turbulence research while avoiding the acoustic time-scale restriction of a fully compressible formulation.
entries.caveat: The low-Mach formulation is unsuitable when shocks or strong acoustic coupling govern the physics. Use the documented model assumptions.

metadata.description: An adaptive mesh hydrodynamics simulation code for low Mach number reacting flows without level sub-cycling.

entries.name: PelePhysics
entries.summary: Supplies thermodynamics, transport, chemistry generation and additional spray, soot and radiation modules shared by Pele solvers. Useful when researching combustion models rather than duplicating property implementations.
entries.caveat: A supporting physics library rather than a complete standalone CFD application; module support differs between Pele solvers.

metadata.description: A collection of physics databases and implementation code for use with the Pele suite of of codes

entries.name: pyJac
entries.summary: Generates analytical Jacobian source code for chemical reaction mechanisms. Helps researchers examine the expensive derivative calculations that arise inside stiff chemical-kinetics integrators and reacting-flow applications.
entries.caveat: An older research tool with version-sensitive dependencies; generated code and mechanism support should be checked in the target environment.

metadata.description: Creates C and CUDA analytical Jacobians for chemical kinetics ODE systems

entries.name: pyMARS
entries.summary: Reduces detailed chemical mechanisms using graph-based methods and sensitivity analysis. Useful for preparing smaller chemistry models when detailed mechanisms make reacting-flow or reactor studies too expensive.
entries.caveat: Reduction accuracy depends on the selected targets and training conditions; validate the reduced mechanism over the intended operating envelope.

metadata.description: Python-based (chemical kinetic) Model Automatic Reduction Software

entries.name: Reaction Mechanism Generator
entries.summary: Constructs chemical kinetic mechanisms using reaction families and thermochemical data. Supports upstream chemistry development for combustion studies before mechanism reduction, reactor assessment or coupling to CFD.
entries.caveat: Generated mechanisms are hypotheses requiring assessment against suitable data; this is not a spatial CFD solver.

metadata.description: Python version of the amazing Reaction Mechanism Generator (RMG).

entries.name: Spitfire
entries.summary: Builds tabulated chemistry models and integrates chemistry or reaction-diffusion systems. Particularly relevant to nonpremixed flamelet libraries used to reduce the cost of larger fire simulations.
entries.caveat: Tables remain specific to their generating assumptions, mechanism and parameter range; extrapolation requires separate assessment.

metadata.description: Spitfire is a Python/C++ library for constructing tabulated chemistry models and solving differential equations.

entries.name: TChem
entries.summary: Provides chemical source terms, thermodynamic properties, Jacobians and canonical reactor formulations for complex kinetic mechanisms. Useful for integrating and studying the stiff chemistry component of reacting simulations.
entries.best_for: Chemical kinetics kernels and reactor models
entries.caveat: Distinguish this kinetics toolkit from the separate TChem-atm atmospheric-chemistry project; it does not supply a complete spatial flow solver.

metadata.description: TChem - A Software Toolkit for the Analysis of Complex Kinetic Models

entries.name: AFiD
entries.summary: Parallel finite-difference flow solver for Rayleigh-Benard convection and Taylor-Couette turbulence, built around distributed decompositions and FFT-based algorithms for large canonical direct numerical simulations on HPC systems.
entries.caveat: Specialized canonical-flow geometry and boundary conditions; check variant-specific documentation and dependencies rather than treating it as a general geometry solver.

metadata.description: A highly parallel application for Rayleigh-Benard and Taylor-Couette flows

entries.name: CaNS
entries.summary: Parallel incompressible Navier-Stokes solver designed for canonical-flow DNS, using a structured finite-difference discretization and efficient pressure solution with CPU and GPU-oriented implementations for turbulence research at scale.
entries.caveat: Targets canonical structured domains; check grid, boundary-condition and accelerator constraints instead of assuming arbitrary industrial geometry support.

metadata.description: A code for fast, massively-parallel direct numerical simulations (DNS) of canonical flows

entries.name: Dedalus
entries.summary: Spectral PDE framework with symbolic equation specification and parallel execution, supporting fluid-dynamics research across Cartesian and curved domains rather than restricting users to one fixed equation set.
entries.caveat: Users formulate equations, gauge conditions and boundary constraints; this flexibility is not a substitute for checking mathematical well-posedness and numerical convergence.

metadata.description: A flexible framework for solving PDEs with modern spectral methods.

entries.name: FluidSim
entries.summary: Python framework for reproducible fluid-dynamics simulations with extensible solvers, MPI-enabled pseudospectral methods, and integrated output and analysis workflows for turbulence and geophysical-flow research across multiple model equations.
entries.caveat: Official publish-only GitHub mirror; canonical development and contributions are on the project's Heptapod Mercurial repository.

metadata.description: :ocean: Framework for studying fluid dynamics with numerical simulations using Python (publish-only mirror). The main repo is hosted on https://foss.heptapod.net (Gitlab fork supporting Mercurial).

entries.name: IAMR
entries.summary: Parallel adaptive-mesh code for variable-density incompressible Navier-Stokes equations, providing an AMReX-based route to locally refined flow simulations and exploration of block-structured algorithms for research applications.
entries.caveat: Variable-density incompressibility is a modeling assumption, not a fully compressible shock-capturing formulation; check the examples and required AMReX revision.

metadata.description: A parallel, adaptive mesh refinement (AMR) code that solves the variable-density incompressible Navier-Stokes equations.

entries.name: incflo
entries.summary: AMReX-based incompressible Navier-Stokes application for flows in complex geometries, combining block-structured adaptive-grid infrastructure with embedded boundaries and shared hydrodynamic utilities for parallel CPU and GPU research.
entries.caveat: Requires compatible AMReX and AMReX-Hydro versions; follow project instructions for supported solvers and boundary conditions rather than assuming general model coverage.

metadata.description: Incompressible Navier-Stokes solver in complex geometries

entries.name: Oceananigans.jl
entries.summary: Julia software for incompressible geophysical fluid dynamics on CPU and GPU hardware, supporting Cartesian and spherical-shell domains, turbulence studies and ocean-oriented models with programmable simulation workflows.
entries.caveat: Ocean-oriented incompressible and hydrostatic/nonhydrostatic modeling assumptions differ from general compressible industrial CFD; choose the documented model appropriate to the scales. Its documented ocean and Boussinesq formulations do not cover arbitrary compressible engineering flows.

metadata.description: 🌊  Julia software for fast, friendly, flexible, ocean-flavored fluid dynamics on CPUs and GPUs

entries.name: OpenSBLI
entries.summary: Python code-generation framework translating symbolic compressible-flow equations into parallel high-order finite-difference solvers, with structured curvilinear multiblock meshes and WENO or TENO shock-capturing options for heterogeneous computing architectures.
entries.caveat: Generated solvers depend on a compatible parallel runtime and compiler stack; changing symbolic equations still requires numerical verification.

metadata.description: A framework for the automated derivation and parallel execution of finite difference solvers on a range of computer architectures.

entries.name: Pencil Code
entries.summary: Modular high-order finite-difference code for compressible hydrodynamics with magnetic fields and particles, offering MPI-parallel infrastructure and many sample configurations for turbulence and astrophysical-fluid research on distributed systems.
entries.caveat: The project documents its own source-management and contribution workflow; numerical diffusion and shock treatment must be selected for the intended regime.

metadata.description: A high-order finite-difference code for compressible hydrodynamic flows with magnetic fields and particles

entries.name: spectralDNS
entries.summary: Python collection of parallel spectral Navier-Stokes and related solvers, providing an inspectable environment for direct numerical simulation and experiments with spectral discretization and time-integration methods.
entries.caveat: Research-oriented solver collection; verify the maintained solver path and current shenfun/MPI dependency compatibility for the intended example.

metadata.description: Spectral Navier Stokes (and similar) solvers in Python

entries.name: WaterLily.jl
entries.summary: Julia solver for unsteady incompressible viscous flow around dynamic immersed bodies, using Cartesian grids, geometric multigrid pressure solves and backend-agnostic CPU or GPU execution in two or three dimensions.
entries.caveat: An immersed Cartesian-grid method rather than a body-fitted mesh solver; quantify boundary and grid-resolution effects for the target geometry.

metadata.description: Fast and simple fluid simulator in Julia

entries.name: Xcompact3d / Incompact3d
entries.summary: High-order compact finite-difference framework for turbulent-flow DNS and LES, combining Cartesian-grid efficiency, distributed-memory parallelism and immersed-boundary treatments for research on incompressible flows and complex geometries.
entries.caveat: The named repository is the CPU solver; inspect the separate accelerator developments rather than assuming identical GPU capabilities.

metadata.description: Current CPU version of our solver for the Navier-Stokes equations

entries.name: CFD Python
entries.summary: A notebook sequence teaching CFD through incremental PDE implementations, culminating in Navier–Stokes exercises. Useful for understanding discretization, numerical diffusion and convergence before adopting larger solver frameworks.
entries.caveat: Educational discretizations and small examples are not production CFD solvers.

metadata.description: A sequence of Jupyter notebooks featuring the "12 Steps to Navier-Stokes" http://lorenabarba.com/

entries.name: CFDBench
entries.summary: Fluid-dynamics surrogate benchmark with cavity, tube, dam and cylinder cases across boundary conditions, geometries and physical properties. Includes datasets and baseline implementations for studying inference-time generalization.
entries.caveat: Original data generation uses commercial ICEM/Fluent; using released data has separate download and storage requirements.

metadata.description: A large-scale benchmark for machine learning methods in fluid dynamics

entries.name: FEniCSx Tutorial
entries.summary: Executable finite-element tutorial covering DOLFINx fundamentals and Navier–Stokes examples. Useful for deriving weak forms, applying boundary conditions and exploring transparent flow implementations with associated explanations and parallel execution.
entries.caveat: Follow the tutorial's supported DOLFINx version; examples are not a universal production flow solver.

metadata.description: A reimplementation of the Springer book: https://github.com/hplgit/fenics-tutorial/, covering new topics as well as transitioning from dolfin to dolfinx

entries.name: Giverny / JHTDB access
entries.summary: Python and MATLAB access tools for querying the Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database. Enables sampled DNS fields and cutouts for turbulence analysis, numerical comparisons and data-driven research without downloading entire simulations.
entries.caveat: Access tokens, query-size limits and available variables depend on the service and chosen dataset.

metadata.description: library for querying the Johns Hopkins Turbulence Database (JHTDB)

entries.name: MASA
entries.summary: Library of manufactured analytical solutions and source terms for PDE software verification. Includes Euler, Navier–Stokes and turbulence-model formulations useful for checking implementation errors and observed convergence orders.
entries.caveat: Manufactured solutions verify equation implementation; they do not validate physical modelling against experiments.

metadata.description: Method of Manufactured Solutions Repository

entries.name: NekExamples
entries.summary: Official Nek5000 examples with case descriptions and required simulation files. Includes canonical and turbulent-flow setups useful for learning spectral-element workflows, inspecting boundary conditions and checking an installation.
entries.caveat: Examples require Nek5000 and case-specific preparation; confirm mesh resolution and expected reference quantities.

metadata.description: Examples for Nek5000

entries.name: PDEBench
entries.summary: Scientific machine-learning benchmark combining PDE datasets, data-generation code and baseline models. Fluid cases and varied initial, boundary and physical parameters support repeatable comparisons of learned flow prediction methods.
entries.caveat: Datasets are hosted separately and can be large; check documented environment and data-path requirements.

metadata.description: PDEBench: An Extensive Benchmark for Scientific Machine Learning

entries.name: preCICE Tutorials
entries.summary: Worked coupled-simulation cases using preCICE with real solvers, including fluid–structure and thermal applications. Useful for understanding participant configuration, adapter interfaces and reproducible multiphysics setup rather than isolated equations.
entries.caveat: Most tutorials need multiple solver installations and adapters with compatible versions.

metadata.description: Various tutorial cases for the coupling library preCICE with real solvers. These files are meant to be rendered on precice.org.

entries.name: Riemann Problems and Jupyter Solutions
entries.summary: Interactive notebook book covering Riemann problems for hyperbolic equations, including acoustics, shallow water and Euler flow. Useful for understanding wave structure and comparing exact or approximate flux solvers.
entries.caveat: Text and executable code have separate license files; consult both when reusing material.

metadata.description: An interactive book about the Riemann problem for hyperbolic PDEs, using Jupyter notebooks.

entries.name: Riemann-Solvers
entries.summary: Compact implementations accompanying classical Riemann-solver methods for advection, Burgers and Euler equations. Useful for comparing schemes and developing intuition about shocks, rarefactions and numerical fluxes.
entries.caveat: No repository-level license was apparent in the inspected listing; inspect permissions before copying code.

metadata.description: Riemann Solvers and Numerical Methods for Fluid Dynamics.

entries.name: SU2 TestCases
entries.summary: Official collection of SU2 test inputs spanning flow, adjoints, conjugate heat transfer and other capabilities. Useful for reproducing regression cases and finding solver-specific examples matched to SU2 development.
entries.caveat: Match the case branch or revision to the SU2 solver version; a regression pass is not physical validation.

metadata.description: Test cases for SU2

entries.name: ADIOS2
entries.summary: Scalable scientific input/output framework transporting self-describing variables through files, networks and memory. Useful for large CFD output pipelines, streaming analysis and reducing coupling between simulation and data consumers.
entries.caveat: Requires integration into the application or an existing compatible I/O path.

metadata.description: Next generation of ADIOS developed in the Exascale Computing Program

entries.name: CGNS
entries.summary: Defines and implements a standard for storing CFD meshes, flow solutions and related metadata. Useful when interoperability and consistent exchange between preprocessing, simulation and postprocessing tools matter.
entries.caveat: A data model and library, not a solver; interoperable use still depends on supported CGNS conventions.

metadata.description: The CFD General Notation System (CGNS) provides a standard for recording and recovering computer data associated with the numerical solution of fluid dynamics equations. All development work and bug fixes should be based off the 'develop' branch, CGNS uses the branching model Gitflow.

entries.name: netCDF4-Python
entries.summary: Python and NumPy interface to the netCDF library. Useful for reading, writing and inspecting array-based simulation datasets, especially geophysical and atmospheric fluid workflows using netCDF conventions.
entries.caveat: Respect netCDF thread-safety limitations and preserve units, coordinates and metadata conventions.

metadata.description: netcdf4-python: python/numpy interface to the netCDF C library

entries.name: ParaView
entries.summary: Scientific visualization application built on VTK, supporting large-data analysis and programmable pipelines. Widely useful for CFD field inspection, slices, streamlines, time histories and reproducible postprocessing workflows.
entries.caveat: Official GitHub mirror; upstream development and issue reporting take place on Kitware GitLab.

metadata.description: VTK-based Data Analysis and Visualization Application

entries.name: PyVista
entries.summary: NumPy-friendly Python interface to VTK datasets, filters and plotting. Supports scripted extraction, slicing and interactive display of CFD meshes and fields in notebooks, applications or automated reporting.
entries.caveat: Headless rendering and remote notebook use may require additional graphics configuration.

metadata.description: 3D visualization and mesh analysis for science and engineering

entries.name: trame
entries.summary: Python framework for interactive scientific web applications, integrating VTK and ParaView rendering. Useful for turning CFD analysis pipelines into browser-accessible viewers with local or remote visualization.
entries.caveat: Application deployment, authentication and resource limits need separate design for public-facing services.

metadata.description: Trame lets you weave various components and technologies into a Web Application solely written in Python.

entries.name: vedo
entries.summary: Python scientific visualization built on VTK and NumPy, with mesh manipulation and analysis helpers. Useful for compact exploratory scripts, interactive inspection and presentation of surfaces or volumetric flow data.
entries.caveat: Check supported readers and field association conventions against the output format of your solver.

metadata.description: A python module for scientific analysis of 3D data based on VTK and Numpy

entries.name: VisIt
entries.summary: Scientific visualization and analysis application for mesh-based simulation data. Useful for exploring large CFD datasets, applying derived quantities and building repeatable analysis routines across supported simulation formats.
entries.caveat: Solver output must match a supported reader or be converted to an appropriate exchange format.

metadata.description: VisIt - Visualization and Data Analysis for Mesh-based Scientific Data

entries.name: VTK
entries.summary: Visualization and data-processing toolkit for building scientific applications. Provides meshes, filters, rendering and file readers that underpin custom CFD postprocessing tools and many established visualization applications.
entries.caveat: A development toolkit rather than a complete end-user CFD application; GitHub is an official mirror.

metadata.description: Mirror of Visualization Toolkit repository

entries.name: yt
entries.summary: Python analysis and visualization for volumetric simulation datasets, including adaptive meshes. Useful for derived fields, spatial selections, profiles and volume rendering in computational astrophysics and related fluid simulations.
entries.caveat: Strongest fit is supported volumetric simulation formats; confirm a frontend exists for your solver.

metadata.description: Main yt repository

entries.name: AMReX
entries.summary: Block-structured adaptive-mesh framework supplying parallel data structures, particles, embedded boundaries and CPU/GPU infrastructure for building CFD applications; it does not provide a single configured flow model.
entries.caveat: Application developers must supply governing equations, discretizations and physical models. Match the framework revision and accelerator configuration to the consuming solver.

metadata.description: AMReX: Software Framework for Block Structured AMR

entries.name: PETSc
entries.summary: Parallel numerical toolkit providing sparse algebra, nonlinear solvers, time integration and distributed meshes for CFD implementations; application code still supplies the flow equations, discretization and boundary conditions.
entries.caveat: Official GitHub mirror; primary development and issue tracking are on GitLab. Solver/preconditioner choices and nullspace handling must match the discretized problem.

metadata.description: Mirror of https://gitlab.com/petsc/petsc

entries.name: hypre
entries.summary: Parallel sparse-system library featuring algebraic and structured multigrid methods, useful for CFD pressure and diffusion solves; it supplies numerical components rather than a turnkey fluid simulation.
entries.caveat: Select an interface and preconditioner appropriate to matrix structure and symmetry; GPU support varies by algorithm and build. Current licensing is Apache-2.0 OR MIT.

metadata.description: Parallel solvers for sparse linear systems featuring multigrid methods.

entries.name: Ginkgo
entries.summary: C++ sparse linear-algebra library targeting many-core CPUs and GPUs, useful inside CFD pressure or coupled-system solvers; users provide matrices and algorithms appropriate to their discretized equations.
entries.caveat: A linear-algebra backend, not a CFD application. Benchmark complete solver convergence and data movement; accelerator support does not guarantee faster end-to-end simulation.

metadata.description: Numerical linear algebra software package

entries.name: MFEM
entries.summary: Modular parallel finite-element library with high-order spaces, adaptive meshes and operator infrastructure for developing CFD discretizations; examples and miniapps are building blocks rather than complete engineering workflows.
entries.caveat: Users select stable spaces, weak forms, boundary conditions and solvers. Reproducing an example does not establish the suitability of a newly assembled flow formulation.

metadata.description: Lightweight, general, scalable C++ library for finite element methods

entries.name: deal.II
entries.summary: C++ adaptive finite-element library providing meshes, finite-element spaces, assembly and parallel algorithms for custom CFD programs, including documented flow examples rather than one universal ready-to-run solver.
entries.caveat: A numerical development library; the application determines governing equations and stable discretization. Optional PETSc, Trilinos and p4est dependencies must be version-compatible.

metadata.description: The development repository for the deal.II finite element library

entries.name: DOLFINx / FEniCSx
entries.summary: C++ and Python finite-element environment for expressing and assembling PDE problems, useful for programmable Navier-Stokes studies; users still formulate weak forms, constraints, boundary conditions and solver strategies.
entries.caveat: DOLFINx is the FEniCSx computational component, not a standalone packaged CFD model. Follow documentation matching the installed release and compatible FEniCSx dependencies.

metadata.description: Next generation FEniCS problem solving environment for solving finite element problems

entries.name: libCEED
entries.summary: Library for factored finite-element operator evaluation across CPU and GPU backends, enabling matrix-free high-order CFD implementations; its algebraic interface integrates into applications rather than defining their complete physics.
entries.caveat: Applications retain mesh, parallel decomposition and solver responsibilities. Backend behavior and deterministic capabilities vary; bundled fluid miniapps illustrate integration rather than certify arbitrary CFD models.

metadata.description: CEED Library: Code for Efficient Extensible Discretizations

entries.name: Kokkos Core
entries.summary: C++ performance-portability programming library abstracting parallel execution and memory layouts, useful for implementing CFD kernels across CPU and GPU architectures; it supplies no governing equations or flow solver.
entries.caveat: Performance portability still requires algorithm, layout and backend choices. Check compiler and device support for the chosen release; numerical correctness remains the application's responsibility.

metadata.description: Kokkos C++ Performance Portability Programming Ecosystem: The Programming Model - Parallel Execution and Memory Abstraction

entries.name: SUNDIALS
entries.summary: Time-integration and nonlinear-solver libraries for differential and algebraic systems, useful for stiff chemistry and semidiscrete CFD equations; applications supply spatial operators, physical models and appropriate solver interfaces.
entries.caveat: Not a spatial CFD solver. Choose tolerances, Jacobians, vector backends and preconditioners for the actual stiffness and conservation requirements; keep package versions consistent.

metadata.description: Official development repository for SUNDIALS - a SUite of Nonlinear and DIfferential/ALgebraic equation Solvers. Pull requests are welcome for bug fixes and minor changes.

entries.name: p4est
entries.summary: Parallel forest-of-octrees library managing adaptive mesh refinement, coarsening and partitioning, useful beneath scalable CFD discretizations; the consuming application supplies numerical fluxes, physical fields and time evolution.
entries.caveat: Mesh infrastructure rather than a flow solver. Official guidance warns that auto-generated GitHub source archives lack required components; use maintained release tarballs or initialize dependencies correctly.

metadata.description: The "p4est" forest-of-octrees library

external.name: Gmsh
external.summary: Geometry construction, mesh generation and post-processing through a desktop interface or scripting APIs, useful for building reproducible CFD meshes and preparing parametric geometry studies.
external.access_note: Canonical development is on ONELAB GitLab. The official site documents GPLv2-or-later terms with a linking exception and separate commercial licensing options.

external.name: Basilisk
external.summary: Provides adaptive Cartesian PDE solvers, interface methods and a large collection of reproducible examples. Its native site combines source, documentation, tests and researcher-contributed simulation cases.
external.access_note: Canonical source is distributed through Darcs. Use the official project pages and source history rather than an arbitrary GitHub mirror.

external.name: OpenFOAM (OpenCFD distribution)
external.summary: Provides the OpenCFD distribution of OpenFOAM with solver, model, meshing and post-processing documentation. Identify this distribution explicitly when choosing compatible tutorials, extensions and case files.
external.access_note: GPLv3 distribution distinct from the OpenFOAM Foundation edition. Follow the official download and version-specific documentation; its development repositories moved to GitLab.com.
